subject: Solaris pilot: premium on-ramp, lead capture, and clawback mechanics
messages:
From: Damien Clark <damien@solaris.ai>
To: logan.wright@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya@solaris.ai>, partners@solaris.ai
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood pilot & commercial model — quick alignment

Hi Logan,

Thanks for taking the time last week. Solaris is excited about an on-ramp pilot for our embedded anomaly-detection SKU bundled with Redwood's hosted inference. Before we lock the pilot scope, a few commercial questions from our side so procurement can greenlight the contract: 

- Lead capture / registration: we need clarity on how co-sell leads will be registered (Portal vs. email), what counts as a qualified lead, and the registration window for retro credits.
- Revenue-share vs referral: for the initial pilot we proposed a 70/30 rev-share in favor of Redwood for platform usage, with a 10% referral top-up to Solaris on closed deals introduced solely by Solaris. Is that acceptable?
- Clawback / churn: if a customer cancels within first 90 days, what clawback applies to partner commissions?
- SKU stacking: if a customer purchases both Solaris and Redwood add-ons, how do you prefer commission sequencing?

I attached a draft MOU with our proposed language (Solaris_MOU_v3.pdf) — highlights on page 2. Can your partner ops review and push a suggested mutual action plan? We're targeting an internal approval call on June 4.

Appreciate a short reply with the Redwood view so I can share with our finance lead.

Cheers,
Damien
VP Partnerships, Solaris AI

Attachment: Solaris_MOU_v3.pdf (PDF, 120KB)
From: logan.wright@redwood.ai
To: Damien Clark <damien@solaris.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood pilot & commercial model — quick alignment

Damien — thanks, and great to hear Solaris is ready to move. Quick answers up front, then a proposed MAP: 

- Lead capture / registration: we prefer registration via our partner portal (portal.redwood.ai/partner-reg) to ensure timestamped entries. Email registration accepted as fallback but requires a confirmation workflow. Qualified lead = company + contact + intent to evaluate within 90 days + budget owner identified. Retro credits allowed for leads registered within 30 days of signed contract (we can extend to 60 for strategic pilots).

- Commercial split: for pilot-only usage we can accept the 70/30 platform rev-share (Redwood 70). The Solaris 10% referral top-up is workable but we need to cap it per-account (suggest $10k cap for pilot). For multi-year committed contracts we prefer moving to a tiered commission (see MAP bullets).

- Clawback: standard policy is pro-rata clawback on partner payouts if the customer cancels within 90 days; full clawback if cancellation within first 30 days. We can consider waiving clawback on early churn for the pilot if Solaris co-funds a portion of onboarding (details below).

- SKU stacking: revenue sequencing is to credit the seller that closed the deal first; if both introduce, split per our standard split matrix (50/50) unless a registration exists.

Proposed mutual action plan (high-level):
1) Week 0 (this week): finalize commercial bullets and MOU redlines.
2) Week 1: partner ops (Marissa) and sales (Karthik) align on registration flow and reporting cadence.
3) Week 2: legal exchange of MSA addendum + pilot SOW (we'll start from Solaris_MOU_v3).
4) Week 3: pilot provisioning + kickoff.

Marissa — can you take partner ops lead on the portal configuration and confirm the retro-credit window?
Karthik — please propose a tiered commission table for post-pilot expansion.

Damien — attaching a short pilot_scope.xlsx template for scope and billing cadence. I'll loop in partner ops and sales to iterate.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Attachment: pilot_scope.xlsx (Excel, 18KB)
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: logan.wright@redwood.ai, Damien Clark <damien@solaris.ai>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood pilot & commercial model — quick alignment

Adding operational detail from partner ops POV. A few clarifying Qs and recommendations: 

1) Registration channel: portal is preferred. For email registrations we'll require: intro email thread, matching Salesforce lead/opp, and partner confirmation email. Retro-credit window recommendation: 45 days for pilots (balances speed with accuracy).

2) Qualified lead definition: add a minimum ARR indicator — recommend >$15k ARR or clear procurement timeline inside 90 days. That prevents small dev-trials from consuming registries.

3) Clawback exceptions: we can waive clawback if Solaris: (a) provides a dedicated enablement credit ($3,500 toward onboarding) and (b) commits to a joint GTM webinar within 60 days. That aligns incentives.

4) SKU stacking execution: if Redwood is primary billing, Redwood pays partner. If Solaris bills, Solaris pays Redwood for platform usage then issues partner payout net of platform; we need to outline invoice routing.

Operational asks for Solaris (for our SOLARIS ID mapping): list of product SKUs, sample invoices for billing routing, and point-of-contact for enablement.

Marissa Cole
Partner Operations
Redwood Inference

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood pilot & commercial model — quick alignment

Damien / team — quick commercial table for post-pilot expansion (draft):

- Pilot: 70/30 to Redwood (platform) with up to 10% Solaris referral top-up, $10k cap per-account.
- Expansion (annualized): Tier 1 (>$250k ARR consumption): 60/40; Tier 2 ($100k–$250k): 65/35; Tier 3 (<$100k): 70/30.
- Registration window for protected credit: 45 days pre-signature (portal) for pilot, 30 days for standard ops.
- Payment terms: Redwood pays partner monthly, net-30 after invoice. Clawback: 100% of partner payout if cancellation within 30 days; pro-rata after.

Open items for legal: whether Solaris referral top-up should be gross or net of discounts and whether caps apply cumulatively or per-deal.

I'll put this in HubSpot under DEAL-2027-0581 and tag partner_ops for tracking.

—Karthik
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Redwood pilot & commercial model — quick alignment

Damien — thanks for the quick review. Summary and next steps below so Solaris procurement has clear asks for the June 4 approval call: 

1) Agreement basics: Redwood agrees to pilot 70/30 rev-share with Solaris referral top-up (10%, $10k cap per-account) for pilot customers.
2) Registration and portal: portal registration preferred; email fallback with SFDC tie required. Retro-credit window for the pilot is 45 days.
3) Clawback: standard 100% within 30 days, pro-rata until 90 days. We can waive clawback for pilot customers if Solaris commits to a $3,500 enablement credit and schedules a joint GTM webinar within 60 days.
4) SKU stacking: invoice routing and sequencing to be captured in SOW.
5) Operational ask from Solaris: please provide product SKU mapping, billing samples, and an enablement POC by June 6.

Attached: updated MOU redlines (we accepted most of your language; highlighted a few changes), plus the filled pilot_scope.xlsx. Once we have Solaris' POC + SKU list, Marissa will configure the portal and open the registration window.

Proposed milestone: legal exchange on June 7; pilot kickoff June 14. If that timeline works for Solaris, we'll mark DEAL-2027-0581 as pilot-ready.

Regards,
Logan Wright
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Solaris_MOU_v3.pdf (redlines, PDF), pilot_scope.xlsx (filled, Excel)
